page: Amazon Web Services c7a.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and does not include a GPU. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with high scores in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also ranks in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core performance is average to weak, as shown by lower Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only bandwidth tests falling into the bottom 25 percent and Passmark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10 percent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7a.large offers a low-cost entry point into dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak memory bandwidth, which limits its effectiveness for memory-intensive applications or database operations. It is best suited for single-threaded compute workloads, basic text processing, and lightweight single-core tasks that do not require high memory throughput or local storage.
